title: Tanzanian Fish Balls
community: Urban coastal Tanzania — street food favourite
author: Chef Fatuma
desc: Tanzanian Kababu ya Samaki — fish balls made from minced fish with onion, coriander, Zanzibar spices, and flour, deep-fried golden and crispy. Served with tamarind sauce and pili pili — the Zanzibar fish street food that outsells everything else.
longDesc: Fish balls are the most popular street food in Zanzibar's Stone Town markets — small, golden, crispy outside and moist within, fragrant with coriander. Eaten in cones of paper with tamarind sauce, standing and talking.
ingredients: // Tamarind dipping: 3 tbsp tamarind paste + 1 tbsp sugar + 2 tbsp water
steps: Mix minced fish with onion, garlic, ginger, coriander, chilli, egg, flour, and spices.
Refrigerate 15 minutes — helps them hold shape.
Fry in batches 4—5 minutes until golden all over.
Make dipping sauce: simmer tamarind, sugar, and water 2 minutes.
Serve immediately with tamarind sauce and pili pili.
chefTips: Do not over-process — some texture is desirable.
commonMistakes: Warm fish mixture — balls fall apart.
cookingScience: The egg and flour create a binding matrix. Chilling firms this matrix before frying. The initial thermal shock from hot oil creates a rapid protein crust that locks the shape permanently.
sustainabilityTips: Can be made from offcuts — sustainable use of the whole fish.
culturalNote: Fish balls are the food of Zanzibar's Stone Town market — bought from a vendor whose family has been frying them in the same spot for generations.
